clue.text: Assemble to do a jigsaw

definitions.meaning: to put parts together into a whole
fitting the cut pieces of a picture back into place

explanation.surface: An instruction to put together a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean joining separate parts into one whole: generally, and literally with puzzle pieces.

clue.text: Get attired in the garment and pose

definitions.meaning: to dress oneself in a piece of clothing
to pretend or exaggerate, as in putting on an act

explanation.surface: Advice to dress up in an outfit and strike an attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both donning clothing and, idiomatically, feigning or showing off.

clue.text: Key reason for arousing passion

parts.note: E is a musical key
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: The main cause of stirring up strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive word or issue is one that stirs strong feeling.

clue.text: Have to get out of bed-admit it

parts.note: to own something is to have it
being up means having risen from bed

explanation.surface: Someone having to rise from bed and confess.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to confess or acknowledge a fault.

clue.text: The Spanish agent resolved to be stylish

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: something resolved is broken down and worked out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish secret agent determined to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' reads as determined, but it signals the anagram of AGENT, giving EGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and stylish are synonyms describing graceful, refined appearance.

clue.text: Abominable man, and one with intelligence

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
I is the Roman numeral for one
nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: A dreadful man who also happens to be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is British informal for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous and abominable are synonyms for something utterly wicked.

clue.text: Tory design never accepted by Socialist bishop

parts.note: the Tories are the party of the political right

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it

parts.note: a red is a socialist or leftist

indicators.note: a design is a pattern made from the letters of the word never, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative plan never accepted by the left wing, mentioning a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' is the anagram signal and 'accepted by' the container. Tories are Britain's Conservative party, on the political right; a red is a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used to address an Anglican bishop is this honorific.

clue.text: Go to work despite disagreement

explanation.surface: Getting down to business even though people disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means start vigorously; as a noun it is a brief fight or argument.

clue.text: Strikers need to have secure marriages

definitions.meaning: things that are struck to make a flame
read as safe pairings of couples

explanation.surface: Industrial strikers want stable marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: These are matches lit by striking on a box, and punningly safe matches between spouses.

clue.text: Bring round payment in advance? Just joking!

indicators.note: the word bring goes round the payment, holding it within

parts.note: taken as written
an ante is a stake paid in before cards are dealt

explanation.surface: Teasing someone about paying up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as a round of drinks paid for, but it is the container: 'Bring' wraps the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantering is teasing, light-hearted talk, the spirit of a playful remark.

clue.text: Claim hard-headed parent has capital

parts.note: to bag something is to claim it

indicators.note: only the head, the first letter, of the word hard is used

parts.note: dad is a father

explanation.surface: A stubborn father has money, to judge by the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard-headed' looks like stubborn, but it gives the head of 'hard'. 'capital' is a capital city: Iraq's.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital city of Iraq.

clue.text: Meet for a session with the tailor

definitions.meaning: suitable or proper, an old adjective
an appointment where clothes are tried on for size

explanation.surface: Meeting a tailor for a session.
explanation.definitionFit: It means appropriate, and also the trying-on of garments being made.

clue.text: Penny has a plan to complete

parts.note: a layout is a plan or arrangement

explanation.surface: Penny has a scheme to finish something.
explanation.definitionFit: To play out a game or scene is to bring it to its finish.

clue.text: Portrait in Gericault's style contains little colour

indicators.note: the clue words contain the letters within them as a continuous run

explanation.surface: A Gericault-style portrait with only a touch of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'portraiT IN GEricault's'; Gericault was a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of a colour.

clue.text: Missed tea brewed up in a cup

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone missed their tea, which was made in a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small coffee cup.

clue.text: Why, this is very midsummer (Twelfth Night)

definitions.text: Why, this is very midsummer (Twelfth Night)

parts.words: Why, this is very midsummer (Twelfth Night)
parts.note: Olivia's line in Shakespeare's comedy finishes with the missing word, describing Malvolio's crazed behaviour

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.walkthrough: Complete the quotation: Olivia calls Malvolio's behaviour 'very midsummer madness'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing word names the insanity that Olivia sees in Malvolio.

clue.text: Versatile fellow takes team into the yard

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the team goes into the yard abbreviation

parts.note: YD is the abbreviation for yard
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A man brings his team into the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with many aspects or talents is versatile.

clue.text: Modern entrance to old prison

parts.note: new means modern
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A new way into a former jail.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a notorious London prison, demolished in 1904.
explanation.definitionFit: Newgate was a historic London jail, now gone.

clue.text: The way uneducated apprentice made pastry

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
rude in its old sense means unlearned or primitive
L stands for a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: How an untrained apprentice baked.
explanation.definitionFit: A strudel is a pastry of thin dough rolled round a filling.

clue.text: Informed of a type of pottery

parts.note: ware is a type of pottery, as in stoneware

explanation.surface: Being told about a kind of ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being informed of something means knowing about it.

clue.text: A large article I left for the maid

parts.note: big means large
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A big object left for the housemaid.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail, from a character in a play, became a generic word for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Eternal appeal of Peter Pan?

definitions.meaning: the boy who never grows up has timeless charm

explanation.surface: Peter Pan's everlasting allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal and never growing older both describe the boy who stays young forever.

clue.text: Where hospital visitors went shortly before?

definitions.meaning: visitors go to the wards of a hospital
near in time, as in nearing evening

explanation.surface: Asking the direction taken by hospital visitors a little earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as TO WARDS it is visitors' destination; as one word it means approaching a time.

clue.text: Rigorous manoeuvres set by the Navy

indicators.note: manoeuvres shift positions, so the letters of set are moved about

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Naval manoeuvres organised with strict discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern and rigorous both mean strict and severe.

clue.text: Not a good-looker

parts.note: a look that is malevolent rather than handsome: a glance believed to bring harm

explanation.surface: Someone who isn't attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good-looker' suggests a handsome person, but it is a look that is not good.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gaze supposed to cast a curse, the opposite of a kindly look.

clue.text: Ambassador needs preparation to get capital cover

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
in golf the address is the stance taken before a stroke

explanation.surface: An ambassador must get ready for a capital city posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means head, so the cover is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover for the head (capital, from Latin caput) is worn as a hat.

clue.text: American objective is correct

parts.note: an end is a goal or objective

explanation.surface: The aim of an American is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or revise.

clue.text: Stimulant for malodorous old sailors

parts.note: smelling means giving off a bad odour
salts are experienced, old seamen

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up for smelly veteran seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pungent ammonia compounds sniffed to revive someone who has fainted.
